findings.summary: Carrying over the previous log's 'Met this goal' choice can pre-check the box, so a new event may qualify the goal without an explicit owner action; this contradicts the ContactEvent qualification invariant and drops the former unchecked default.
findings.evidence: screen.logContact: "channel, depth and the Met this goal choice carry over" (removed: "Met this goal defaults unchecked") vs entity.ContactEvent invariant: "Qualifies only when the owner explicitly marks that it met this goal"; J.contact/c5: "optionally mark Met this goal"

findings.summary: The journey puts the form-prefill behaviour on step c4, which is a branch decision on screen.person, while the form itself is on screen.logContact in step c5.
findings.evidence: J.contact/c4: "Log what happened? The form opens prefilled from the previous log", stepScreen screen.person; J.contact/c5 stepScreen screen.logContact

findings.summary: The hook fixture now covers log-form prefill, but the criterion it verifies still claims only composition, state and keyboard checks, so the hook and its criterion no longer match.
findings.evidence: hook fixture: "protected browser fixture over all screens incl. log-form prefill" vs C.webapp.screen.exact claim: "checks loaded, empty, loading, error and validation compositions, login continuation and keyboard actions"
